subagent_input.last_assistant_message:
I've completed the adversarial fact-check of the claim "Ghostty supports the kitty graphics (image) protocol, and it works through tmux."

**Verdict: REFUTED (high confidence)** — as an overreach/oversimplification of the cited quote.

Breakdown:
- **First half TRUE**: Ghostty officially supports the kitty graphics protocol (confirmed via ghostty.org/docs/features and DeepWiki; pinned + Unicode-placeholder placements; only animation unsupported).
- **Second half "works through tmux" is the problem**: The cited quote itself contains the qualifier "BUT the data has to be encoded correctly." It does NOT work through tmux by default — tmux filters the kitty APC sequences. It only works as a "hack" requiring all of: `allow-passthrough on`, app-side DCS passthrough wrapping, and Unicode placeholders; and it breaks in nested tmux.
- **The cited thread (#7224) is itself a failure report**, and pi-mono issue #2374 (March 2026, Ghostty 1.3.1 + tmux 3.6a) confirms images still don't render without app-side DCS passthrough.
- **Source quality**: forum discussion making a strong generalized claim that the same forum heavily qualifies — insufficient for the unconditioned phrasing.

The burden is on the CLI tool (e.g., kitten icat, timg) to implement tmux passthrough — not something Ghostty alone delivers.
